title: Apartment building collapses after explosion, fire in Glace Bay, N.S.
summary: Cape Breton Regional Municipality say 17 people were reported injured in the early morning incident, and it's not clear yet if there were any fatalities.

image.caption: A fire has destroyed a building on Commercial Street in Glace Bay, N.S. (Submitted by Ernie Bagnell)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·Updated
Cape Breton Regional Municipality say 17 people were reported injured in the early morning incident, and it's not clear yet if there were any fatalities.
17 people reported injured in early morning incident in Cape Breton Regional Municipality
Crews from several fire departments in Cape Breton are on the scene of a building collapse and structure fire in Glace Bay, N.S., that injured 17 people.
The explosion happened around 6 a.m. on Wednesday at Pizza 67, a local pizzeria. The front of the building at 130 Commercial St. collapsed, said Cape Breton Regional Police.
The force of the explosion broke windows on nearby structures.
Shortly afterward, a fire started in the building, which has the pizza shop on the ground floor and about 20 apartments on the upper level.
Crews from more than a half-dozen fire departments responded to the incident. (Ernie Bagnell)
Cape Breton Regional Municipality spokesperson Christina Lamey said 17 people had minor injuries, and 14 of them were transported to Glace Bay Hospital.
Lamey said it is still unclear if there were any fatalities.
"The activity that's currently underway is to try to ascertain how many people were actually in the building," she said.
"We of course know of the 17 people that were assessed early in the morning but it will take some time to ascertain if everybody had made it out of the building."
A CBC reporter on the scene said most of the building has collapsed, and the structure was left with only one wall standing.
The explosion happened at 6 a.m. on Wednesday. (Ernie Bagnell)
Crews from seven or eight fire departments responded to the incident, as well as police and paramedics.

Ernie Bagnell, who lives in Glace Bay, was out early this morning grabbing a coffee when he spotted smoke downtown and drove to the scene. By that time, he said, the front of the building had collapsed.
"The firemen were there on top of it, up in the air, everywhere, trying to put it out, sirens in the distance," he said.
Lamey said as of 11 a.m., crews are still fighting the blaze, watering the site and an excavator is moving debris.
Crews working on a ladder truck fight the fire. (Ernie Bagnell)
The building is located near the intersection of Main Street and is next door to the Savoy Theatre.
Lamey said there are several street closures in the downtown area, and people are being asked to stay away from the area to allow emergency responders to do their work.
A comfort centre has opened at the Glace Bay Miners' Forum for building residents.
Lamey said it's too early to know what caused the explosion, collapse or fire.
